title: Passaging Adherent Cancer Cell Lines
author: Emily Souster
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgtbjwin

steps.title: Remove Old Media
steps.instruction: Remove the old culture media from the flask using a sterile aspirator pipette.

steps.title: Wash Cells
steps.instruction: Gently wash the cells with PBS, adding reagents to the side/back of the flask initially to avoid dislodging cells.

substeps.instruction: Add PBS volume as recommended in Table 1, column B
Aspirate the PBS from the flask

steps.title: Detach Cells with TrypLE
steps.instruction: Apply TrypLE Express Enzyme to detach the cells from the flask surface.

substeps.instruction: Add sufficient TrypLE Express Enzyme to cover the bottom of the flask (see Table 1, column C for volume)
Rock the flask to ensure the TrypLE covers the cell surface
Incubate the flask at 37 °C for 3-5 minutes
Check cell detachment via microscope; if necessary, tap the side of the flask or return to the incubator until all cells have detached

steps.title: Neutralize and Collect Cells
steps.instruction: Stop the enzymatic reaction and collect the cell suspension into a sterile tube.

substeps.instruction: Add fresh media to the flask at a volume equal to the TrypLE added
Use the liquid to rinse cells off the bottom of the flask
Transfer the entire volume to an appropriately sized sterile tube

steps.title: Centrifuge Cell Suspension
steps.instruction: Spin the cells to concentrate them into a pellet.

substeps.instruction: Spin the tube at 300 x g for 3 minutes
Ensure tubes are spun inside centrifuge buckets with sealed safety caps
Transfer the sealed bucket to a microbiology safety cabinet before removing the tubes

steps.title: Resuspend Cell Pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells in fresh media.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet
Resuspend the pellet in an appropriate volume of fresh media (around 5 mL - 20 mL)
Mix well to ensure a single cell suspension

steps.title: Perform Cell Count
steps.instruction: Determine the cell concentration if required.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 100 µL of cell suspension
Count using the preferred method

steps.title: Seed Cells into New Flask
steps.instruction: Transfer the cell suspension to a new flask to achieve the desired split ratio or cell number.

substeps.instruction: Add fresh media and an appropriate volume of cell suspension to a new flask
Aim for total volumes of media and cells as recommended in Table 1, column D (e.g., 24 mL for a T150 flask or 12 mL for a T75 flask when splitting 1:2)

steps.title: Add Selection Agent
steps.instruction: If maintaining a selected population of Cas9 cells, add blasticidin.

substeps.instruction: Determine desired concentration via 'Blasticidin titration of cancer cell lines' protocol
Add the required volume of 10mg/ml blasticidin based on flask size (Table 2)

steps.title: Incubate and Distribute Cells
steps.instruction: Place the flask in the incubator and ensure cells are evenly distributed.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the flask to a 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator
Agitate the flask gently back and forth and side to side

steps.title: Maintain Culture
steps.instruction: Monitor and maintain the cell culture daily.

substeps.instruction: Inspect cells daily and record confluency
Perform a complete media change twice per week, or as needed if media appears yellow
